Body: Businesses must disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal information collected about consumers, the sources of that information, the business purposes for collecting or selling it, and the categories of third parties with whom the information is shared.

Consumers have the right to request deletion of their personal information, subject to certain exceptions. Businesses must delete information from their records and direct service providers to delete the information.

Consumers have the right to opt-out of the sale or sharing of their personal information. Businesses must provide a clear and conspicuous link on their homepage titled 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information'.

Consumers have the right to correct inaccurate personal information that a business maintains about them, taking into account the nature of the personal information and the purposes of the processing.

Requirement: Right to Limit Use of Sensitive Personal Information
Body: Consumers have the right to limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information to only what is necessary to perform services or provide goods reasonably expected by the consumer.
Privacy policies must describe the categories of personal information collected and the purposes for which the categories are used. This must be updated at least once every 12 months.

Privacy policies must disclose whether the business sells or shares personal information and provide a separate link titled 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' on the homepage if applicable.

Businesses must provide notice at or before the point of collection informing consumers of the categories of personal information to be collected and the purposes for which the categories will be used.

If a business sells or shares personal information, it must provide notice to consumers of their right to opt-out and include a link on the homepage titled 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information'.

If offering financial incentives in exchange for personal information, businesses must provide notice of the material terms of the financial incentive program and how the value of personal information is calculated.

Businesses must limit collection, use, retention, and sharing of personal information to what is reasonably necessary and proportionate to achieve the purposes for which it was collected or processed.
Personal information collected for disclosed purposes shall not be further collected, used, or disclosed for incompatible purposes unless notice is provided to the consumer.
Businesses shall not retain personal information for each disclosed purpose for which the personal information was collected for longer than is reasonably necessary for that purpose.

Sensitive personal information includes Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, account credentials, precise geolocation, racial/ethnic origin, religious beliefs, health data, sex life/orientation, and genetic data. Special handling and opt-out rights apply.

Businesses must implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices appropriate to the nature of the personal information to protect it from unauthorized access, destruction, use, modification, or disclosure.

Service providers must implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices, assist businesses in meeting their CCPA obligations, and certify they understand restrictions on retention, use, and disclosure.
In the event of unauthorized access to personal information, businesses must provide notice of the breach to affected consumers and implement security measures to prevent further breaches.

Businesses must establish procedures to verify the identity of consumers making requests to know or delete personal information, using methods reasonably designed to ensure the requester is the consumer or authorized representative.
Businesses must respond to verified consumer requests within 45 days of receipt. This period may be extended by an additional 45 days when reasonably necessary, with notice to the consumer.

Businesses cannot discriminate against consumers for exercising their CCPA rights, including denying goods/services, charging different prices, or providing different quality of goods/services, unless the difference is reasonably related to value.

Businesses must honor requests made through authorized agents if the consumer provides signed permission or power of attorney. Businesses may require verification from both the agent and the consumer.
Contracts with service providers must prohibit the service provider from retaining, using, or disclosing personal information for any purpose other than performing services specified in the contract.
Businesses must disclose in their privacy policy the categories of personal information disclosed for business purposes and the categories of third parties to whom information is disclosed.
Selling includes disclosing personal information to third parties for monetary or other valuable consideration. Businesses must track and disclose all sales or sharing of personal information.
Businesses must not sell or share personal information of consumers under 13 years of age unless they obtain affirmative authorization (opt-in consent) from the child's parent or guardian.
Businesses must not sell or share personal information of consumers between 13 and 16 years of age unless the consumer affirmatively authorizes (opts in to) the sale or sharing.
Personal information collected in the employment or B2B context has modified requirements under CCPA. Certain exemptions applied until January 1, 2023, when full CPRA requirements took effect.
Privacy policies must be accessible and easy to read. They should be made available on the business's website and mobile app if applicable, using a clear and conspicuous link.

Businesses must provide two or more designated methods for submitting requests to know and delete, including at minimum a toll-free telephone number and a website address if the business operates a website.

The 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link must be clear and conspicuous on the homepage of the business's website. For mobile apps, the link must be accessible from the app settings menu or homepage.
Businesses must maintain records of consumer requests and how they responded for at least 24 months. This includes verification methods used and the consumer's requests.
Businesses must compile metrics regarding consumer requests and make them available in their privacy policy or on their website, including number of requests received, complied with, and denied.
Privacy policies must be updated at least once every 12 months and whenever there are material changes to the business's privacy practices that affect consumers.
Businesses should train employees who handle consumer inquiries about the business's privacy practices and how to direct consumers to exercise their rights under CCPA.
